newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-MAKELELE BECOMES MARSEILLE'S SIXTH NEW RECRUIT.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MAKELELE BECOMES MARSEILLE'S SIXTH NEW RECRUIT.

text.p: France international Claude Makelele is Marseille's sixth new recruit as the former European Cup winners try to recapture past glory.
Marseille struck a 12 million francs ($2 million) deal with Nantes on Thursday night for the transfer of the midfielder, who made his debut for France against Sweden in April.
The Mediterranean club also signed Bordeaux captain and defender Patrick Colleter for two years and defensive midfielder Frederic Brando from Le Havre for four on Thursday.
Makelele, who began his career at Brest and joined Nantes in 1992, is expected to sign a three-year contract which includes a release clause after one season.
Colleter follows Marseille-born coach Rolland Courbis from Bordeaux. Marseille agreed to Courbis's terms of a one-year contract two weeks ago.
Central defender Serge Blanc was Marseille's first recruit at the end of a disappoiting first season back in the first division when he joined from Montpellier.
They have also secured the services of Montenegrin forward Miladin Becanovic, who scored 13 league goals for relegated Lille this season, and defender William Gallas from Caen, also down.
Marseille are still looking for a libero and a forward, who could both be leading foreign players, as they try to improve on their mid-table position and no away victories in the season just ended.
Several members of the current squad are expected to leave, including Italian defender Alberto Malusci and Bulgaria midfielder Yordan Lechkov. Both have been transfer-listed.
"The players are subject to the law of offer and demand," Courbis said.
Defender Ivan Francheschini returns to Parma after spending a season on loan from the Italian club.
